newsitem.title: CHINA: China airlines cut fares for foreigners in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China airlines cut fares for foreigners in 1997.

text.p: Chinese aviation authorities have slashed domestic air fares for foreigners travelling in China to try to boost tourism, the China Daily newspaper said on Tuesday.

"Overseas travellers who book airline flights to China and then travel in the country will enjoy more discounted air ticket prices in China this year," it quoted Bao Peide, deputy director of the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), as saying.

The administration had cut air fares for domestic flights by 30 percent in the off seasons from January 1 to March 31 and in December, Bao said. Airlines would offer a 20 percent discount in the peak season from April 1 to November 30, Bao said.
"The number of overseas tourists is estimated at more than 40 million and a considerable number of them will fly on Chinese airlines," Bao said.
The reductions were aimed at drawing more foreign tourists to China this year as part of a year-long "Visit China '97" promotional campaign, he said.
Foreigners travelling in China pay higher prices for air tickets than Chinese citizens.
